scoring.formula: raw[axis] = sum(mult * effect[axis]); max[axis] = sum(abs(effect[axis])); score[axis] = 100 * (max + raw) / (2 * max)

meta.presentation: Stored grouped by axis for maintainability. The app must SHUFFLE at runtime with a fixed seed so consecutive items do not come from the same axis.

questions.text: Biological race is the deepest and most decisive fact determining a people's character and destiny.
Racial purity is a value worth protecting through active state policy.
A nation's strength ultimately rests on the biological quality of its people.
Mixing of distinct races weakens the character and vitality of a nation.
Some races are naturally suited to rule and others to be ruled.
Blood and descent, not shared institutions, are what truly define who belongs to the nation.
What defines the nation is shared culture, language, and history, not biology or bloodline.
Anyone who fully embraces the nation's culture and struggle should be considered part of it, regardless of ancestry.
Racial theory is a distraction from the real basis of national unity, which is cultural and political.
The nation is a spiritual and cultural community, not a biological category.
Racial hierarchy has no legitimate place in a properly ordered nationalist movement.
National unity should be built on shared struggle and loyalty, not on ancestry.
Big finance and large capital are enemies of the nation as much as any external threat.
Interest-bearing capital and speculative finance should be broken and subordinated to national production.
A national revolution has to expropriate parasitic capital, not just discipline it.
Workers' material interests must be genuinely served, not just rhetorically invoked, by a nationalist movement.
Class privilege within the nation is as much an enemy as class privilege serving foreign interests.
The nation's revolution is incomplete if it leaves the existing economic elite untouched.
The nation's existing industrialists and business elite can be valuable allies against common enemies.
Private capital, properly aligned with national goals, should be preserved and used, not expropriated.
A strong national economy needs the cooperation of existing business elites, not their elimination.
Radical economic levelling threatens the social order a nationalist movement is trying to defend.
A movement that alienates capital and industry weakens itself for no strategic gain.
National strength is better built through alliance with existing economic power than through its destruction.
The nation's spiritual life should draw on pre-Christian myth and will, not on the churches.
Established religious institutions have grown too weak and universalist to serve as the nation's spiritual centre.
A national movement's true religion is the nation and the race, not any confessional church.
Clerical authority should be subordinated to the movement's own vision, not the reverse.
Christianity's emphasis on universal brotherhood conflicts with a movement built on national or racial struggle.
The state, not the church, should be the ultimate spiritual authority for the nation.
The nation's traditional church should be honoured as a pillar of the social order, not sidelined.
A movement should work with, not against, established religious authority and its institutions.
Religious faith and clerical support give a nationalist movement legitimacy it cannot generate on its own.
The clergy's moral authority should be respected and incorporated into the movement's public life.
A nationalist movement should present itself as the defender of traditional religion, not its rival.
Confessional loyalty and national loyalty should reinforce, not compete with, each other.
Existing conservative institutions and elites are useful, if limited, allies for restoring order.
An authoritarian government that preserves the social hierarchy is preferable to a mass revolutionary party.
Order and stability, delivered from above by a strong executive, matter more than mass mobilisation.
Working through existing institutions, even undemocratically, is more realistic than remaking society from below.
A traditional elite, properly empowered, can restore national order without needing a mass party apparatus.
Authoritarian rule that leaves most of society's structure intact is a workable and sufficient model.
The nation needs total mobilisation of society through a single mass party, not just an authoritarian government.
Every institution of society — youth, labour, culture — should be brought under the movement's organisation.
A revolutionary party has to permeate the whole of society, not just occupy the state.
Passive obedience to an authoritarian state is not enough; the population must be actively mobilised and organised.
The party, not the traditional state apparatus, should be the true centre of national life.
A totalising mass movement, not a conventional authoritarian government, is what national rebirth requires.
The nation's vitality is proven and renewed through expansion and the conquest of living space.
A great people is entitled to secure territory beyond its current borders by force if necessary.
National greatness naturally expresses itself in imperial ambition, not just self-defence.
Weaker neighbouring peoples and territories are legitimate objects of national expansion.
A nation that does not expand when it has the strength to do so is failing its own destiny.
War and conquest are not aberrations but expressions of a nation's vital strength.
The nation's goal should be securing and defending its existing homeland, not conquering new territory.
Expansionist ambition beyond the nation's own people and territory is a needless and costly overreach.
A defensive nationalism, focused on the homeland, is more sustainable than an expansionist one.
Foreign conquest drains the resources a movement needs to consolidate power at home.
National rebirth doesn't require empire; it requires securing what is already the nation's own.
A movement should renounce expansionist ambitions and focus entirely on domestic renewal.
The nation is reborn through myth, will, and struggle, not through rational administration alone.
A movement needs a unifying myth of national rebirth that goes beyond rational political argument.
Ritual, symbol, and collective ecstasy are legitimate and necessary tools of national mobilisation.
The leader's will and the nation's myth matter more to political success than technical policy.
A politics of pure rational calculation cannot generate the devotion a national movement needs.
Heroic struggle and sacrifice, not bureaucratic competence, define the movement's true character.
The movement's legitimacy should rest on efficient, rational administration of the state, not on myth or ritual.
Technocratic competence matters more to national strength than symbolism or collective myth.
A modern nationalist movement should present itself in the language of expertise and order, not mystical rebirth.
Practical results, not evocations of destiny or myth, are what actually build durable national strength.
Rational planning and administrative efficiency should take priority over appeals to myth and will.
A movement's success depends more on competent governance than on stirring collective symbolism.
The economy should be organised into corporate bodies representing employers and workers together under state coordination.
Sectoral councils, not direct state ministries, should manage the day-to-day running of industry.
Class conflict should be replaced by structured cooperation between capital and labour within each industry.
Corporatist bargaining bodies are a more stable economic model than either free markets or direct state control.
Organising the economy by trade and sector, rather than treating individuals as isolated units, better reflects the nation's organic structure.
A syndicalist structure of national production keeps economic decisions close to the industries themselves.
The state itself, not intermediary corporate bodies, should directly command and coordinate the economy.
Direct state control of production is more reliable than delegating economic coordination to sectoral councils.
Corporatist intermediary bodies dilute the authority the state needs to direct the nation's economy effectively.
A command economy run straight from the centre avoids the compromises corporatist bargaining requires.
Sectoral councils tend to become new vested interests that the state has to work around.
Centralised state command of production is the more disciplined and reliable economic model.
Technology, industry, and speed are expressions of the nation's vitality and should be embraced and celebrated.
A modern nationalist movement should present itself as futurist, not nostalgic for a rural past.
Industrial power and technological progress are sources of national strength worth actively pursuing.
The movement should associate itself with modernity, machines, and industrial dynamism.
A backward-looking, agrarian ideal has less to offer national renewal than embracing industrial modernity does.
Speed, machinery, and industrial production symbolise the nation's rebirth better than rural tradition does.
The nation's true character lies in its agrarian, pre-industrial roots, not in industrial modernity.
Industrial modernity has uprooted the nation from the soil and traditions that gave it strength.
A return to rural, traditional ways of life is central to genuine national renewal.
The movement should resist, not celebrate, the rootless and mechanised character of modern industrial life.
National rebirth means recovering a traditional, land-based way of life, not accelerating industrial modernity.
Urban, industrial modernity is a foreign imposition on the nation's authentic agrarian character.
